tibetan:
ཐོག་མ་དབུས་མཐའ་རྣམ་པར་སྤངས། །ཆུ་ཤིང་བཞིན་དུ་སྙིང་པོ་མེད། །དྲི་ཟའི་གྲོང་ཁྱེར་འདྲ་བ་སྟེ། །རྨོངས་#པའི་གྲོང་ཁྱེར་མི་བཟད་#པའི། །འགྲོ་བ་སྒྱུ་མ་བཞིན་དུ་སྣང་། །ཚངས་སོགས་འཇིག་རྟེན་འདི་ལ་ནི། །བདེན་པར་རབ་ཏུ་གང་སྣང་བ། །དེ་ནི་འཕགས་ལ་{བརྫུན་,རྫུན་}#ཞེས་གསུངས། །
འདི་ལས་གཞན་ལྟ་ཅི་ཞིག་ལུས། །འཇིག་རྟེན་མ་རིག་ལྡོངས་གྱུར་པ། །སྲེད་པ་རྒྱུན་གྱིས་རྗེས་འབྲང་#དང་། །མཁས་པ་སྲེད་པ་དང་བྲལ་བ། །དགེ་བ་རྣམས་ལྟ་ག་ལ་མཉམ། །དེ་ཉིད་ཚོལ་ལ་ཐོག་མར་ནི། །ཐམས་ཅད་ཡོད་ཅེས་བརྗོད་པར་བྱ། །དོན་རྣམས་རྟོགས་ཤིང་ཆགས་མེད་
ལ། །ཕྱིས་#ནི་རྣམ་པར་དབེན་པའོ། །རྣམ་པར་དབེན་དོན་མི་ཤེས་ལ། །ཐོས་པ་ཙམ་ལ་འཇུག་བྱེད་ཅིང་། །གང་དག་བསོད་ནམས་མི་བྱེད་པ། །སྐྱེས་བུ་ཐ་ཤལ་དེ་དག་བརླག །ལས་རྣམས་འབྲས་བུ་བཅས་ཉིད་དང་། །འགྲོ་བ་དག་ཀྱང་ཡང་དག་བཤད། །དེ་ཡི་རང་བཞིན་ཡོངས་
ཤེས་དང་། །སྐྱེ་བ་མེད་པ་དག་ཀྱང་བསྟན། །དགོས་པའི་དབང་གིས་རྒྱལ་བ་རྣམས། །ང་དང་ང་ཡི་ཞེས་གསུངས་#ལྟར། །ཕུང་པོ་ཁམས་དང་སྐྱེ་མཆེད་རྣམས། །དེ་བཞིན་དགོས་པའི་དབང་གིས་གསུངས། །འབྱུང་བ་ཆེ་ལ་སོགས་བཤད་པ། །རྣམ་པར་ཤེས་སུ་ཡང་དག་འདུ། །
དེ་#ཤེས་པས་ནི་འབྲལ་འགྱུར་ན། །ལོག་པར་#རྣམ་བརྟགས་མ་ཡིན་ནམ། །མྱ་ངན་འདས་པ་བདེན་གཅིག་པུར། །རྒྱལ་བ་རྣམས་ཀྱིས་གང་གསུངས་པ། །དེ་ཚེ་ལྷག་མ་ལོག་མིན་ཞེས། །མཁས་པ་སུ་ཞིག་རྟོག་པར་བྱེད། །ཇི་སྲིད་ཡིད་ཀྱི་རྣམ་གཡོ་བ། །དེ་སྲིད་བདུད་
ཀྱི་སྤྱོད་ཡུལ་དེ#། །དེ་ལྟ་ཡིན་ན་འདི་ལ་ནི། །ཉེས་པ་མེད་པར་ཅིས་མི་འཐད། །འཇིག་རྟེན་མ་རིག་རྐྱེན་ཅན་དུ། །གང་ཕྱིར་སངས་རྒྱས་རྣམས་གསུངས་པ། །འདི་ཡི་ཕྱིར་ན་འཇིག་རྟེན་འདི། །རྣམ་རྟོག་ཡིན་ཞེས་ཅིས་མི་འཐད། །མ་རིག་འགགས་པར་གྱུར་པ་ན། །གང་ཞིག་
འགག་པར་འགྱུར་བ་དེ། །མི་ཤེས་པ་ལས་ཀུན་བརྟགས་པར། །ཇི་ལྟ་བུར་#ན་གསལ་མི་འགྱུར། །གང་ཞིག་རྒྱུ་དང་བཅས་འབྱུང་ཞིང་། །རྐྱེན་མེད་པར་ནི་གནས་པ་མེད། །རྐྱེན་མེད་ཕྱིར་ཡང་འཇིག་འགྱུར་བ། །དེ་ནི་ཡོད་ཅེས་ཇི་ལྟར་རྟོགས། །གལ་ཏེ་ཡོད་པར་སྨྲ་བ་རྣམས། །

Completely devoid of beginning, middle, or end.
Like a plantain tree, they have no core.
They are like a city of <term>gandharvas</term> <gloss>celestial musicians; a metaphor for a mirage</gloss>.
The world, a terrible city of confusion,
Appears like a magical illusion.

What appears as truth to this world,
Including Brahma and the others,
The Noble Ones call "false."
What else remains but this?

The world is blinded by ignorance
And follows the current of craving.
How could the wise, free from craving,
Be the same as those who seek virtue? <note>referring to those seeking ordinary virtuous rebirth versus ultimate liberation</note>

To those searching for suchness, one should first
Say that "everything exists."
Once they understand the meanings and are without attachment,
Then later they are taught "solitude" <gloss>emptiness</gloss>.

Without knowing the meaning of solitude,
Those who merely follow what they have heard,
And who do not perform merit,
Those inferior people are ruined.

The fact that actions have results
And the realms of existence were also correctly taught.
The thorough knowledge of their nature
And their non-arising were also shown.

Just as the Victors spoke of "I" and "mine"
For the sake of a specific purpose,
So too the aggregates, elements, and sense-bases
Were taught for a specific purpose.

What was described as the great elements and so on
Is perfectly gathered within consciousness.
Since one is freed by knowing that,
Is it not falsely conceptualized?

The Victors have taught
That nirvana is the sole truth.
At that time, what wise person would think
That the rest is not false?

As long as the mind is wavering,
That is the domain of <term>Mara</term> <gloss>the tempter or personification of death and desire</gloss>.
If that is so, then why is it not logical
That there is no fault in this?

Because the Buddhas have taught
That the world has ignorance as its condition,
Why is it not logical that this world
Is a conceptualization?

When ignorance ceases,
That which ceases along with it—
How could it not be clear
That it was conceptualized from not knowing?

That which arises together with a cause
And does not remain without conditions,
And also perishes because of the absence of conditions—
How can it be understood to "exist"?

If those who speak of existence
Remain attached to the excellence of things,
head: They arise entirely from the cause of ignorance,
tail:
Remaining on that very path,
There is nothing wonderful about that.
old_translation:
<meta>continues from previous page</meta>
It is free from beginning, middle, and end. It is without essence, like a plantain tree. It is like the city of the <term>gandharvas</term> <gloss>celestial musicians; a mirage</gloss>. The world appears like a magical illusion to the city of the deluded. 

That which appears as true to this world of Brahma and so on, is said to be false to the Noble Ones. Apart from this, what else remains? 

The world is blinded by ignorance and follows the current of craving. How could the wise, who are free from craving and possess virtue, be equal to them? 

To those seeking reality, one should first say "Everything exists." Once they have realized the meaning and are without attachment, then one speaks of "isolation." 

Those who do not know the meaning of isolation, but engage only in what they have heard and do not perform merit—those inferior men are ruined. 

The fact that actions have results and the realms of existence were perfectly explained. The thorough knowledge of their nature and their non-arising were also shown. 

Just as the Victors spoke of "I" and "mine" for a necessary purpose, so they spoke of the aggregates, elements, and sense bases for a necessary purpose. 

The explanation of the great elements and so on is perfectly included within consciousness. If one is freed by knowing that, is it not then falsely conceptualized? 

Since the Victors said that nirvana is the sole truth, what wise person would conceptualize the rest as not being false? 

As long as the mind wavers, it is the domain of <term>Mara</term> <gloss>the Tempter/Delusion</gloss>. If that is so, why is it not tenable that there is no fault in this? 

Because the Buddhas said that the world is conditioned by ignorance, why is it not tenable that this world is a conceptualization? 

When ignorance is ceased, that which ceases—how could it not be clear that it was conceptualized from not knowing? 

That which arises with a cause and does not remain without conditions, and which perishes when conditions are absent—how can it be understood as "existing"?
